senses.gloss: m., pl. קָקוּלֵי, קָקוּלִין (= קלקול׳; קלל) a sort of cress used by the poor (cardamum or nasturtium, Löw, Pfl. 349).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 3:1:6">Y. Erub. III, 20ᵈ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 8:4:4">Y. Peah VIII, 21ᵃ</cite> top, expl. <cite ref="Q01392"><he>פעפועין</he></cite>.—

<cite ref="Pesachim 114a:3">Pes. 114ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>דאכיל אליתא טשי בעליתא דאכיל קקולי אקיקלי וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>קילקולא אקילקולי</he>) he that eats fat-tail will have to hide himself (before his creditors) in the loft, who eats cress may rest quietly by the dunghill of the town.
